title: O Thou, Enthroned in Worlds Above
description: O Thou, Enthroned in Worlds Above in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 440 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Lord's Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou, en-throned in worlds a-bove, Our Fa-ther and our Friend! Lo, at the foot-stool of thy love, Thy child-ren hum-bly bend.

lines: O Thou, enthroned in worlds above,
Our Father and our Friend!
Lo, at the footstool of thy love,
Thy children humbly bend.
All reverence to thy name be given;
Thy kingdom wide displayed;
And, as thy will is done in heaven,
Be it on earth obeyed.
Our table may thy bounty spread,
From thine exhaustless store,
From day to day with daily bread, —
Nor would we ask for more.
That pardon we to others give,
Do thou to us extend;
From all temptation, Lord, relieve;
From every ill defend.
And now to thee belong, Most High,
The kingdom, glory, power,
Through the broad earth and spacious sky,
Both now and evermore.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
